title: Jittered loadbook: occupancy & variance log
content:
Purpose
This note captures exploration of noise and variance in throughput experiments. Goal: define a small, repeatable set of jittered-load experiments that expose GPU occupancy sensitivity and scheduler interactions that the steady-state harness misses.

Background / motivation
- Our canonical harness produces steady uniform QPS ramps and long steady windows. That is great for baseline throughput but misses transient behaviors that matter in production: short bursts, inter-request jitter, heterogeneous prompt lengths, and scheduler preemption.
- Recent customer cases showed occasional 2–5% throughput regressions under bursty traffic even though steady-state tests passed. We need a targeted methodology to reproduce and explain the variance.

High-level idea
- Add controlled randomness (jitter) to arrival times and prompt-length distributions to simulate real-world noise.
- Measure GPU occupancy, CUDA kernel launch counts, PCIe stalls, and CPU-side queuing. Correlate occupancy variance with throughput drops and tail latency spikes.
- Use small randomized experiment batches (30–90s each) with seeds to probe behavior space while keeping runs short and repeatable.

Key experiment knobs
- mean_qps: baseline QPS (e.g., 50, 200, 500)
- jitter_sigma_ms: standard deviation of inter-arrival Gaussian jitter (e.g., 0, 5, 20, 100 ms)
- burst_ratio: fraction of requests grouped into spikes (0–0.5). A spike groups N extra requests within a 50 ms window.
- prompt_mix: vector of prompt token-length classes, e.g., [short: 1–20, medium: 21–128, long: 129–512], percentages adjustable.
- seed: RNG seed for repeatability (record explicitly).

Load generator config (example, pseudo-yaml inline)
- { test_name: jitter-200qps-sigma20-burst10pct, mean_qps: 200, jitter_sigma_ms: 20, burst_ratio: 0.1, prompt_mix: {short:50,medium:40,long:10}, seed: 88431 }

Measurement policy
- Warmup: two phases
  1) kernel priming: 30s of low-qps synthetic prompts that touch model layers to ensure CUDA kernels JIT/CUFFT/etc. are initialized (esp on fresh containers)
  2) stochastic warmup: 60s run using the target mean_qps but with jitter_sigma_ms=10 to avoid all-requests-align artifact
- Sampling windows: run experiments in 60s measurement windows, ignore first 10s of each window, and collect metrics for remaining 50s
- Repeat: each config should be repeated with 5 different seeds and once with seed held constant to assert seed-level repeatability

Metrics to capture (and cadence)
- Application metrics (per-request): request_id, prompt_len, queuing_time, service_time, per-token-time, total_latency
- GPU metrics (NVML sampling at 500ms): GPU utilization %, memory utilization MB, SM occupancy estimate (if available), GPU power
- Kernel metrics: kernel launch rate, time-in-kernel cumulative (from CUPTI/profiler sampling)
- Host metrics: CPU load per core, thread blocked time, context-switch rate
- System events: OOM/killed, GC triggered, process preemption, node-level scheduling events

Repeatability checklist (practices)
- Fix seeds and record them in test metadata. Use RNG only for arrival times and prompt selection; keep other components deterministic.
- Ensure no background cron/backup/monitor jobs on test nodes. Use dedicated placement (dedicated test pool) where possible.
- Pin loadgen and server processes to cores (taskset) and isolate via cgroups to avoid noisy neighbor CPU interference.
- Use the same container image and driver stack; record driver and CUDA versions in metadata.

Observed failure modes (notes from pilot runs)
- Case A: sigma=0 (no jitter), steady 200 QPS: high measured GPU utilization (~92%), consistent throughput.
- Case B: sigma=20ms, 10% bursts: frequent short tail latency spikes; occupancy oscillates between 60% and 95% on 500ms NVML samples. Hypothesis: short bursts create hot kernel launches separated by small gaps, preventing kernels from running with fully-packed CTAs and underutilizing tensor cores.
- Case C: long-tail prompts introduced buffer allocation spikes on the host leading to GC/allocator stalls; these align with throughput dips.
- Case D: warmup omitted: first minute shows higher kernel launch overhead and higher per-token times; subsequent minutes amortize but leads to noisy initial window.

Quick root-cause signals to look for
- Low SM occupancy during bursts -> kernel launch overhead dominating (look at kernel cumtime vs wall)
- High host CPU sys time and context-switches -> CPU scheduling stalls feeding the GPU
- PCIe rx/tx spikes -> data-transfer serialization causing delays between kernels

Mitigations tried (and results)
- Pre-warm kernels with targeted low-latency prompts -> reduced initial kernel-launch overhead by ~40% (pilot)
- Increase batch coalescing window slightly (10–30ms) when jitter present -> improved SM occupancy but increased median latency by ~3% (tradeoff)
- CPU pinning reduced context-switch rate and reduced variance across runs

Experiment log summary (selected runs)
- run-2025-02-12-01: mean_qps=200, sigma=0, occupancy steady, throughput 19.8k tokens/s, notes: baseline
- run-2025-02-12-02: mean_qps=200, sigma=20ms, burst_ratio=0.1, occupancy oscillating, throughput 18.6k tokens/s, notes: tail spikes correlate with low occupancy samples
- run-2025-02-14-03: same as 02 but with CPU pinning -> throughput 19.3k tokens/s, tail spikes reduced

Open questions / next steps
- How does occupancy variance scale with model size? Need matrix across 1B/7B/70B models (smaller models might be more sensitive to arrival jitter).
- Can we instrument a lightweight kernel coalescing heuristic in the runtime that detects short-burst patterns and temporarily relaxes the batching window? Risk: higher median latency. Prototype idea: if burstiness detected and queue depth low, open window by +10ms for next 100ms.
- Validate whether PCIe serialization is a significant contributor on multi-card nodes by enabling NVLINK-only tests and comparing.

Commands / reproducibility notes
- loadgen invocation (abbreviated): ./loadgen --config tests/jittered/200qps-s20-b10.json --seed 88431 --report-dir /tmp/logs/jitter-200-s20
- nvml sampler: python tools/nvml_sampler.py --interval 0.5 --out /tmp/logs/nvml-jitter-200.csv
- record driver: nvidia-smi --query-gpu=driver_version,cuda_version --format=csv

Quick TODOs (owner tags)
- [Emily] formalize config schema and add to repo tests/jittered/ (high priority)
- [Marco] implement deterministic prompt selector with seed logging (medium)
- [Asha] run 1B/7B matrix and capture occupancy traces (medium)
- [Jordan] prototype adaptive coalescer in the runtime (spike)
Notes to self
- Keep runs short and increase sample count rather than long single runs when exploring noise space. Short runs make it cheaper to sweep seeds/configs.
- When sharing results, include a small reproducible bundle: config, seed, nvml log, loadgen output. That made the last investigation quick to debug.

Appendix: short checklist for running a jittered occupancy test
- allocate a clean node (no background jobs)
- note CUDA/driver versions and container image
- copy tests/jittered config + seed into report dir
- start nvml sampler, then start loadgen
- wait measurement window + collect artifacts

End of note.
